clue.text: Awful stain on cover causes talk

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the following letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A dreadful mark on a book jacket or cushion gets everyone gossiping.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is spoken exchange between people, so talk is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Canada initially, then America not a melting pot, perhaps

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
not tells us the following small word is to be taken away from the country name
melting loses its shape, so the remaining letters run together in a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of Canada
taken as written
the article, removed from the country name

explanation.surface: A remark that North America, Canada first, is not after all the famous melting pot of cultures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Melting pot' reads as one phrase about immigration, but the words split: 'melting' signals the shuffle and 'pot, perhaps' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot made of fired clay is one example of ceramic ware, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Requirement came first, but created irritation

blocks.note: a requirement is a need
whoever came first in a race led it

explanation.surface: Someone who put their needs first ended up annoying everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to annoy or provoke them, so needled means caused irritation.

clue.text: Formerly in use, now out of commission?

blocks.note: ex- is the prefix for former
something in service is in use

explanation.surface: An old machine that used to be working is now broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: A commission is also an officer's rank in the armed forces, so someone 'out of commission' has left the military.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex-service describes veterans who formerly served in the armed forces, which a commissioned officer leaves on retiring.

clue.text: One who was good and erect?

blocks.note: a saint was a good person, abbreviated ST
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about someone virtuous who held themselves upright.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to set it upright, which is to erect or put it up.

clue.text: Sack, perhaps, because betting system takes hold

blocks.note: the tote is a pool-betting system run at British racecourses
to bag something is to seize or take hold of it

explanation.surface: Someone is fired because the racecourse betting operation takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismissal from a job, but it is the carrying sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A tote bag is a large open carrier bag, and a sack is one kind of such bag.

clue.text: Suspect caring nothing for what concerns living things

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are not in their true order

blocks.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is suspected of not caring at all about the natural world.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic means relating to or derived from living organisms, as in organic chemistry.

clue.text: Composer has role re-written for female - one who is free

indicators.note: a part re-written has its letters set down again in a different order

blocks.note: J S Bach, the German composer
taken as written
a girl is a female

explanation.surface: A composer reworks an opera part so a woman can sing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor girl is an independent unmarried young woman, free of any husband.

clue.text: Close without a song

blocks.note: an air is a tune or song
less can mean without, as in 'a year less a day'

explanation.surface: An instruction to end a performance without singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb meaning finish; it is the adjective for stuffy weather or rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather or rooms are stuffy and lacking fresh air, which is what airless means.

clue.text: A tug in a bad way in the Caribbean

definitions.note: names the island by where it is

indicators.note: something in a bad way is in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the four words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tugboat is struggling in Caribbean waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a bad way' reads as one phrase, but 'in a' belongs to the letters and 'bad way' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is an island nation located among the Leeward Islands of the West Indies.

clue.text: Perfect love, but extreme frigidity!

blocks.note: absolute means perfect or complete
love is a score of nothing in tennis

explanation.surface: A romance that seems ideal but is chilly in the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute zero is the lowest temperature physically possible, about minus 273 Celsius, the ultimate cold.

clue.text: More lowly than Uriah Heep?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone even more servile than Dickens's fawning clerk
setter's reading: Heep drops his aitches and calls himself 'umble, so the comparative with the aitch restored is what we want

explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep, in Dickens's David Copperfield, endlessly claims to be 'very 'umble', dropping the H.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of humble means of lower rank or more meek, so it means more lowly.

clue.text: Exposes the claims of French beds

blocks.note: de is French for of
bunks are narrow beds

explanation.surface: Someone reveals the truth about French beds and their supposed qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk is to show that an idea or belief is false or exaggerated.

clue.text: Clear when detectives follow clue, missing both first and last

indicators.note: dropping the opening and closing letters leaves only the inner ones
follow places the detectives after the other piece

blocks.note: the inner pair of clue
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives working from a clue that has lost its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means easily understood and expressed plainly, the sense of clear prose.

clue.text: The Italian record (one note by a student) doesn't make sense

blocks.note: il is Italian for the
a log is a written record
the Roman numeral for one
C is a musical note
taken as written
a learner, as on the L-plates of a British learner driver

explanation.surface: An Italian record that features a single note from a learner makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a predicate: 'X doesn't make sense' and 'X is illogical' say the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illogical lacks sound reasoning, so it doesn't make sense; the definition is a verb phrase for an adjective.

clue.text: Period of animation looks set for some in the House of Lords

definitions.text: some in the House of Lords

blocks.note: a life is the span of time a thing is alive or animate
to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A long stretch of liveliness seems destined for some members of the upper chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Life peers are members appointed to Britain's House of Lords whose titles are not passed to heirs.

clue.text: Cook gets a complaint about the joint

blocks.note: to roast is to cook in an oven
beef is slang for a grievance

explanation.surface: A chef receives a grumble about the meat being served.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint is a large cut of meat for roasting, and roast beef is the classic British Sunday one.

clue.text: She is a woman speaking beautiful French

indicators.note: speaking tells us to go by how the French word is said rather than spelt

blocks.note: Anna is a woman's name
belle is French for beautiful

explanation.surface: A woman who speaks fine French is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Annabel is a girl's given name, so it stands for a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Some Puritan trickery concerning a particular Hindu movement

indicators.note: some of the following words means just a part of their run of letters is needed

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Puritans accuse a Hindu sect of deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantric relates to the tantras, esoteric texts and practices of a school of Hinduism and Buddhism.

clue.text: Overheated? Massage back, not extremities!

indicators.note: back means the word for massage is read in the opposite direction
extremities are the outermost ends, so only the end letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: to massage is to rub
the two end letters of not

explanation.surface: A massage instruction: work on the back, but leave the hands and feet alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Massage back' reads as rubbing someone's back; 'back' is the reversal signal, and 'not extremities' means the ends of the word not.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is burnt has been cooked at too high a temperature, hence overheated.

clue.text: Familiar business, sort of rare and becoming very odd

indicators.note: sort can be a verb, to arrange, so the letters are sorted into a new order

blocks.note: biz is informal slang for business, as in showbiz
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-known company is becoming unusual and strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre describes something strikingly strange or unconventional, an intensified version of odd.

clue.text: Rock movers?

blocks.note: surface reading: people or machines that shift boulders
setter's reading: rock is the music, so these are crew who move a band's gear

explanation.definitionFit: Roadies are the touring crew who set up and transport the equipment of rock bands.

clue.text: Batsmen's turn to get prizes without their opener

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and without it means that letter is removed

blocks.note: winnings are money or prizes won

explanation.surface: Cricketers take their turn to win awards, minus the opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' sounds like cricket's opening batsman, but here it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an innings is a team's or player's period of batting.

clue.text: Brush around the plant

indicators.note: around suggests letters moved about from their places into another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sweep the floor of the factory or round a pot plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody bush, one kind of garden plant.

clue.text: Sparkle given off by pizza put before two sleeping characters

indicators.note: put before places the food item ahead of the remaining piece

blocks.note: taken as written
zz is the cartoon sign for snoring

explanation.surface: A pizza is so lively it glitters next to two dozing people.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizzazz is lively flair and glamour, the quality of sparkle in a person or show.

clue.text: Manual worker in US city moved right

blocks.note: Los Angeles
bore is the past of bear, to carry or move
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A labourer relocated to an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' does double duty: it makes the city LA and warns that the answer takes the American spelling, without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: A laborer does physical, unskilled work with the hands, which is what manual work means.

clue.text: Peer and I join the Queen beforehand

blocks.note: an earl is a nobleman, a peer
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A nobleman and I meet the monarch ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier as an adverb means at a previous time, the same as beforehand.

clue.text: These popular films can be highly explosive

definitions.note: adjective standing for the noun: things that are highly explosive

blocks.note: first meaning: big commercial hit movies
second meaning: huge aerial bombs from the Second World War

explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' in film talk means a sensational hit, but here it is literal: the name was first given to bombs able to flatten a city block.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockbuster was a massive wartime bomb, and the term then passed to hugely successful films.
